title: Summary, review and chapter test
competency: Review the unit and take the timed chapter test.

keywords.def: The study of how chemical reactions and electricity are converted into each other.

en.text: Redox reactions transfer electrons from a reducing agent to an oxidizing agent. Electrolytic cells use electricity to drive non-spontaneous reactions, and Faraday's laws give the amounts formed. Galvanic cells use spontaneous reactions to make electricity: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode, ΔG° = −nFE°, and the Nernst equation handles non-standard concentrations. Batteries, fuel cells and corrosion are everyday electrochemistry.

screens.title: Unit summary
paras: Oxidation: loss of e⁻; reduction: gain of e⁻; they happen together.
Electrolytic cell: anode (+), cathode (−); electricity drives a non-spontaneous reaction.
Galvanic cell: anode (−), cathode (+); E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode > 0 for a spontaneous reaction.
Corrosion is a short-circuited galvanic cell; galvanizing and cathodic protection stop it.

items.text: The process in which a compound absorbs electrical energy and decomposes into its elements is
opts: A. electrolysis
B. solvolysis
C. hydrolysis
D. electroplating
items.why: Electrolysis uses electrical energy to drive a non-spontaneous redox reaction, e.g. 2NaCl(l) → 2Na(l) + Cl₂(g). Solvolysis and hydrolysis are reactions with the solvent/water, not driven by electricity. Electroplating is one application of electrolysis (coating a metal with another metal), not decomposition into elements.

items.text: Which of the following is true about galvanic cells used in commercial lead storage batteries? In lead storage batteries,
opts: A. galvanic cells are connected in series.
B. galvanic cells are connected in parallel.
C. half of galvanic cells are connected in series.
D. half of galvanic cells are connected in parallel.
items.ans: A. galvanic cells are connected in series.
items.why: Each Pb/PbO₂/H₂SO₄ cell gives about 2 V. A 12 V car battery has six such cells connected in series, so their voltages add: 6 × 2 V = 12 V. Parallel connection (B, D) would keep the voltage at 2 V; C ('half in series') does not describe a real battery.

items.text: What is the purpose of synthetic cryolite in the extraction of aluminum by the Hall's process?
opts: A. Cryolite increases the purity of the extracted aluminum.
B. Cryolite reduces the melting point of alumina.
C. Cryolite increases the melting point of alumina.
D. Cryolite is used as a catalyst in the extraction of aluminum.
items.ans: B. Cryolite reduces the melting point of alumina.
items.why: Pure alumina (Al₂O₃) melts at about 2045 °C — too costly to keep molten. Dissolving it in molten cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) lowers the working temperature to about 950–1000 °C and improves conductivity. A is not its role (purity comes from purified bauxite); C is the opposite; D is wrong — cryolite is a solvent, not a catalyst.

opts: A. the addition of hydrogen to a substance and removal of oxygen from a substance.
B. the loss of electrons by a species, accompanied by an increase in oxidation number.
C. the addition of electron(s) to the oxidizing agent.
D. the reduction of the oxidation state of oxidizing agent.
items.ans: B. the loss of electrons by a species, accompanied by an increase in oxidation number.
items.why: Oxidation = loss of electrons = increase in oxidation number (e.g. Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻, 0 → +2). A describes reduction (gain of H / loss of O). C and D describe what happens to the oxidizing agent, which is itself REDUCED.

items.text: What is meant by preferential discharge, if a number of ions are present in a solution? It means that the one requires
opts: A. least energy will be liberated first at a given electrode.
B. least energy will be liberated last at a given electrode.
C. highest energy will be liberated first at a given electrode.
D. highest energy will be liberated last at a given electrode.
items.ans: A. least energy will be liberated first at a given electrode.
items.why: When several ions can be discharged at one electrode, the one needing the least energy (lowest discharge potential) is discharged first. Example: electrolysis of dilute NaCl(aq) — at the cathode H₂ forms rather than Na, because H⁺/H₂O is reduced more easily. The choice also depends on concentration and electrode type, but B, C and D reverse the energy rule.

opts: A. passing the same quantity of electricity through solutions of different electrolytes produces masses of substances that are directly proportional to their molecular masses.
B. passing the same quantity of electricity through solutions of different electrolytes produces masses of substances that are directly proportional to their equivalent masses.
C. the amount of substance consumed or produced at an electrode is directly proportional to the quantity of the electricity passing through the solution.
D. the amount of substance consumed or produced at an electrode is inversely proportional to the quantity of electricity passing through the solution.
items.ans: B. passing the same quantity of electricity through solutions of different electrolytes produces masses of substances that are directly proportional to their equivalent masses.
items.why: Second law: for the same charge Q, m₁/m₂ = E₁/E₂, where equivalent mass E = molar mass / electrons per ion. Example: same charge deposits Ag (E = 108) and Cu (E = 63.5 ÷ 2 = 31.75) in the ratio 108 : 31.75. A uses molecular (molar) mass, ignoring ion charge; C is Faraday's FIRST law (m ∝ Q); D reverses the first law.

items.text: Which of the following is true about a Zn–Cu voltaic cell?
opts: A. The anode half-cell consists of Cu electrode dipped into a Cu²⁺ solution.
B. After the cell runs for several hours, the Zn electrode weighs less.
C. The electrons flow from right to left through the external circuit.
D. As the cell operates, electrons are continuously generated at the cathode and consumed at the anode.
items.ans: B. After the cell runs for several hours, the Zn electrode weighs less.
items.why: Zn is more easily oxidised (E° = −0.76 V) than Cu (E° = +0.34 V), so Zn is the anode: Zn(s) → Zn²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻. Zn atoms go into solution, so the zinc electrode loses mass (B); Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu deposits on the cathode. A is wrong (Cu/Cu²⁺ is the cathode). D reverses the electrodes: electrons are produced at the anode and used at the cathode. C depends on how the cell is drawn; by the usual convention (anode on the left) electrons flow left to right.

items.text: Why is CaCl₂ added to NaCl in a 1 : 1½ ratio in the Downs cell for the manufacturing of sodium metal?
opts: A. CaCl₂ is used as a catalyst.
B. CaCl₂ is used to lower melting temperature of NaCl.
C. CaCl₂ is used to lower density of the mixture.
D. CaCl₂ is used as an electrolyte.
items.ans: B. CaCl₂ is used to lower melting temperature of NaCl.
items.why: Pure NaCl melts at about 801 °C; the CaCl₂–NaCl mixture melts at about 600 °C. Running at lower temperature saves energy and reduces loss of volatile sodium. CaCl₂ is not a catalyst (A); it does not serve to lower density (C); the electrolyte being decomposed is NaCl (D).

items.text: Which one of the following galvanic cells is an example of a secondary cell?
opts: A. Leclanché dry cell
B. Zinc–carbon dry cell
C. Daniell cell
D. Lead storage cell
items.why: A secondary cell can be recharged: passing current backwards reverses the cell reaction. Lead storage battery: Pb + PbO₂ + 2H₂SO₄ ⇌ 2PbSO₄ + 2H₂O (discharge →, charge ←). Leclanché and zinc–carbon dry cells (the same cell) are primary (not rechargeable); the Daniell cell is a laboratory primary cell.

items.text: Which one of the following is responsible for electrolytic conductivity?
opts: A. Electrons held in a fixed position.
B. Movement of ions.
C. Ions strongly held in a fixed position.
D. Free electrons.
items.why: In an electrolyte (molten salt or solution) the charge carriers are mobile ions: cations move to the cathode, anions to the anode. D (free electrons) is metallic conduction. A and C describe charges that cannot move (e.g. a solid ionic crystal does not conduct).

items.text:
Which one of the following is the reducing agent in the following reaction?
8NH₃(g) + 6NO₂(g) → 7N₂(g) + 12H₂O(l)
opts: A. H₂O
B. N₂
C. NO₂
D. NH₃
items.why: Oxidation numbers of N: NH₃ = −3, NO₂ = +4, N₂ = 0. N in NH₃: −3 → 0, an increase → NH₃ is oxidised, so it is the reducing agent. N in NO₂: +4 → 0, a decrease → NO₂ is reduced, so it is the oxidizing agent (C). H₂O and N₂ are products, not agents.

items.text: Which one of the following is TRUE about the electrolysis of a molten hypothetical electrolyte, MX?
opts: A. Electrons are not transferred from one species to the other.
B. The overall reaction is a redox reaction.
C. X is produced at the negative electrode.
D. M is produced at the anode.
items.ans: B. The overall reaction is a redox reaction.
items.why: Molten MX contains M⁺ and X⁻ ions. Cathode (negative): M⁺ + e⁻ → M (reduction). Anode (positive): 2X⁻ → X₂ + 2e⁻ (oxidation). Overall 2MX → 2M + X₂ is a redox reaction driven by electrical energy (B). A is false (electrons are transferred via the external circuit). C is false: X forms at the positive electrode. D is false: M forms at the cathode.

items.text: One of the basic differences between metallic conduction and electrolytic conduction is:
opts: A. The charge carriers in metals are localized electrons while strongly held ions are in electrolytic conduction.
B. The conduction of electricity is due to the movement of ions in metallic conduction while the flow of mobile electrons in electrolytic conduction.
C. The conduction of electricity is due to the movement of ions in electrolytic conduction while the flow of mobile electrons in metallic conduction.
D. The charge carriers in metals are cations and anions while mobile electrons are in electrolytic conduction.
items.ans: C. The conduction of electricity is due to the movement of ions in electrolytic conduction while the flow of mobile electrons in metallic conduction.
items.why: Metals: delocalised (mobile) electrons carry the charge; no chemical change occurs. Electrolytes: mobile cations and anions carry the charge, and chemical changes (redox) occur at the electrodes. A says the carriers are localized/strongly held — then nothing could conduct. B and D swap the carriers.
